kill_argument: The paper asks the reader to trust one narrow negative result as its only clean capability anchor, but that anchor is still internally inconsistent. The introduction states a paired GSM8K 200-example control (sections/intro.tex:28-34). The body then repeatedly describes the same control as a random 50-problem subset (main_eai_body.tex:564, 587, 636, 1588, 1640, 1737), while elsewhere calling it the same N=200 held-out slice (main_eai_body.tex:385, 645, 1590, 1656, 1735; ethics_statement.tex:392). Worse, the reconciliation paragraph labels it both a paired control and a one-sample test against the base (main_eai_body.tex:643-646). A hostile reviewer can therefore say the paper's central empirical anchor is not auditable.
critical: The single clean held-out GSM8K control still has two incompatible sample sizes and two incompatible test descriptions: 200 at sections/intro.tex:29, main_eai_body.tex:385,645,1590,1656,1735, ethics_statement.tex:392; 50 at main_eai_body.tex:564,587,636,1588,1640,1737. main_eai_body.tex:643-646 also says paired and one-sample for the same analysis.
major: The toy arithmetic cross-library baseline is still in the main Results (main_eai_body.tex:509-549) and remains promoted in the statistical appendix tables (sections/stat_rigor_updates.tex:87-104), which invites a toy-task inflation rejection line.
The stack-sensitivity headline still depends on only two real cross-stack runs while verl and OpenRLHF remain dry-run placeholders (sections/abstract_eai.tex:12-14, main_eai_body.tex:490-492).

Bibliography cleanup is not submission-grade: duplicate works and malformed entry types remain, so Vancouver compliance is not fully clean (references.bib:237-256, 542-583, 776-789, 1195-1200, 1435-1440, 1599-1604).
minor: High-overlap slogan-like sentences remain and are worth rewriting before Turnitin.

Most likely EAI width hotspots are tab:main_results_stats (sections/stat_rigor_updates.tex:60-84), tab:ppo_grpo_stats (sections/stat_rigor_updates.tex:141-156), tab:results_gsm8k_stats (sections/stat_rigor_updates.tex:114-138), tab:results_arithmetic_stats (sections/stat_rigor_updates.tex:87-104), and tab:heldout_gsm8k (main_eai_body.tex:605-631).

plagiarism_flags.quote: The algorithm label alone is an under-specified experimental treatment; usable signal must be verified per stack.
This paper audits a group-relative RL runner inspired by GRPO, not a canonical GRPO reproduction.
The familiar p_x > 1/G rule is only an expected-one-success heuristic; it is not a threshold theorem.
The mixed-group probability formula is the explanatory core; ZVF/GU is the operational interface.
The paper's main contribution is therefore diagnostic.
A bare 'PPO versus GRPO' comparison is not an interpretable scientific claim.
